descriptionChirho: The word by which a person, place, or thing is known and called — the core meaning of Hebrew shem (Arabic cognate ism), covering personal names, place names, divine Name, naming acts, and all inflected forms with articles, possessive suffixes (his/her/their/my/our name), construct chains (name-of X), and prepositional prefixes (by/for/to/in/like/from the name), as well as plural forms used in genealogies, census rolls, and enumeration lists (names of the sons of X, by their names).

The extended sense of shem meaning fame, reputation, or renown — used of distinguished persons ('men of name' = men of renown, Gen 6:4, Num 16:2), of a king or warrior whose fame has spread, and of making oneself a name; distinguished in Swahili by sifa (reputation) and mashuhuri (famous) rather than jina (name), and in Spanish by renombre rather than nombre.
